name: Eugene Onegin
author: Alexander Pushkin
description: Eugene Onegin appears in Eugene Onegin by Alexander Pushkin as a Protagonist. Archetype of the 'superfluous man' in Russian literature
personality: Cynical, bored, sophisticated, emotionally detached, world-weary
arc: Rejects Tatyana's love, later regrets it when she rejects him
significance: Archetype of the 'superfluous man' in Russian literature

name: Tatyana Larina
author: Alexander Pushkin
description: Tatyana Larina appears in Eugene Onegin by Alexander Pushkin as a Female lead. Ideal of Russian womanhood; moral strength
arc: From naive romantic to dignified married woman who chooses duty over passion
significance: Ideal of Russian womanhood; moral strength

name: Pechorin
author: Mikhail Lermontov
description: Pechorin appears in A Hero of Our Time by Mikhail Lermontov as a Protagonist. Embodies the 'superfluous man'; psychological complexity
personality: Cynical, manipulative, intelligent, bored, self-destructive, Byronic
arc: Moves through encounters leaving destruction, unable to find meaning

name: Chichikov
author: Nikolai Gogol
description: Chichikov appears in Dead Souls by Nikolai Gogol as a Protagonist. Satirizes Russian bureaucracy and corruption
personality: Cunning, opportunistic, adaptable, superficially charming, greedy
arc: Travels buying 'dead souls' for fraudulent scheme

name: Akaky Akakievich
author: Nikolai Gogol
description: Akaky Akakievich appears in The Overcoat by Nikolai Gogol as a Protagonist. Symbol of the little man crushed by society
personality: Meek, poor, dedicated clerk, simple, socially invisible
arc: Obsesses over new coat, loses it, dies of grief, returns as ghost
significance: Symbol of the little man crushed by society

name: Bazarov
author: Ivan Turgenev
description: Bazarov appears in Fathers and Sons by Ivan Turgenev as a Protagonist. Embodiment of nihilism and generational conflict
personality: Nihilistic, rational, arrogant, principled, rejects tradition and emotion
arc: Challenges old values, falls in love (contradicting his beliefs), dies of typhus
significance: Embodiment of nihilism and generational conflict

name: Rodion Raskolnikov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Rodion Raskolnikov appears in Crime and Punishment by Fyodor Dostoevsky as a Protagonist. Exploration of moral philosophy, guilt, and redemption
personality: Proud, isolated, intellectual, conflicted, tormented, philosophical
arc: Murders pawnbroker to test theory, consumed by guilt, finds redemption through love
significance: Exploration of moral philosophy, guilt, and redemption

name: Sonya Marmeladova
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Sonya Marmeladova appears in Crime and Punishment by Fyodor Dostoevsky as a Supporting. Symbol of Christian redemption and unconditional love
personality: Compassionate, self-sacrificing, faithful, humble, prostitute forced by poverty
arc: Guides Raskolnikov toward redemption through faith and love
significance: Symbol of Christian redemption and unconditional love

name: Prince Myshkin
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Prince Myshkin appears in The Idiot by Fyodor Dostoevsky as a Protagonist. Exploration of innocence and goodness in a fallen world
personality: Innocent, compassionate, epileptic, Christ-like, naive, pure-hearted
arc: Tries to bring goodness to corrupt society, fails, returns to madness
significance: Exploration of innocence and goodness in a fallen world

name: Nastasya Filippovna
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Nastasya Filippovna appears in The Idiot by Fyodor Dostoevsky as a Female lead. Tragedy of damaged innocence
personality: Beautiful, traumatized, proud, self-destructive, torn between love and vengeance
arc: Cannot accept love, chooses self-destruction, murdered

name: Pierre Bezukhov
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: Pierre Bezukhov appears in War and Peace by Leo Tolstoy as a Protagonist. Tolstoy's voice on meaning of life
personality: Idealistic, philosophical, searching for meaning, clumsy, sincere
arc: From aimless wealthy heir to man finding purpose through suffering and love
significance: Tolstoy's voice on meaning of life

name: Natasha Rostova
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: Natasha Rostova appears in War and Peace by Leo Tolstoy as a Female lead. Embodiment of life force and Russian spirit
personality: Vivacious, emotional, impulsive, loving, vital, transforms through experience
arc: From spirited girl to mature woman and mother
significance: Embodiment of life force and Russian spirit

name: Prince Andrei Bolkonsky
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: Prince Andrei Bolkonsky appears in War and Peace by Leo Tolstoy as a Major character. Exploration of pride, death, and meaning
personality: Proud, ambitious, disillusioned, intelligent, searching for glory
arc: Seeks glory in war, finds it hollow, finds peace before death
significance: Exploration of pride, death, and meaning

name: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: Anna Karenina appears in Anna Karenina by Leo Tolstoy as a Protagonist. Tragedy of passion vs societal duty
personality: Passionate, impulsive, loving, trapped by society, increasingly desperate
arc: Leaves husband for lover, rejected by society, descends into jealousy and despair, suicide
significance: Tragedy of passion vs societal duty

name: Konstantin Levin
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: Konstantin Levin appears in Anna Karenina by Leo Tolstoy as a Parallel protagonist. Tolstoy's voice on authentic life
personality: Philosophical, sincere, searches for meaning, loves nature and work
arc: Finds meaning in family, work, and faith

name: Ivan Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Ivan Karamazov appears in The Brothers Karamazov by Fyodor Dostoevsky as a Major character. Intellectual rebellion against God
personality: Intellectual, atheistic, tormented by doubt, cold, rationalist
arc: Questions God's justice, suffers mental breakdown after father's murder

name: Dmitri Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Dmitri Karamazov appears in The Brothers Karamazov by Fyodor Dostoevsky as a Major character. Embodiment of passion and Karamazov sensuality
arc: Accused of patricide, accepts suffering as redemption
significance: Embodiment of passion and Karamazov sensuality

name: Alyosha Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Alyosha Karamazov appears in The Brothers Karamazov by Fyodor Dostoevsky as a Youngest brother. Dostoevsky's ideal of Christian love
personality: Pure, loving, faithful, compassionate, novice monk
arc: Maintains faith despite suffering, spreads love

name: Ilya Oblomov
author: Ivan Goncharov
description: Ilya Oblomov appears in Oblomov by Ivan Goncharov as a Protagonist. Symbol of Russian inertia and wasted potential
personality: Lazy, dreamy, passive, kind-hearted, paralyzed by inaction
arc: Cannot leave his couch, loses love, dies unfulfilled
significance: Symbol of Russian inertia and wasted potential
